narrative.overview: The Citum design system reflects the quiet authority of a museum reading room: restrained, editorial, and built for sustained attention. It replaces the prior 'Scholarly Workshop' system with a paper-and-hairline palette, square corners, and a single disciplined accent color.

rules.name: The Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: Never use pure white (#fff) for large background areas. Use the wall tone (#FBFBF9) as the base; reserve paper (#FFFFFF) for framed plates and cards set against it.

rules.name: The Single-Accent Rule
rules.body: Navy is the only color that means 'interactive.' Oxide never appears on anything clickable — it marks marginalia details only (figure numbers, margin-note markers, small rules).

rules.name: The Border-First Rule
rules.body: Hairline borders are the primary method of separation. Shadow is reserved for plates that need to read as physically framed and lifted off the wall.

rules.name: The Margin Asymmetry Rule
rules.body: On wide screens, break the single reading column with a narrow Tufte-style margin-note rail rather than symmetric multi-column grids.

rules.name: The Direct Naming Rule
rules.body: Section headings and UI labels are literal ('Four examples,' 'Who it's for,' 'Install,' 'On CSL,' 'News'). Never metaphorical framing like 'exhibits' or 'wall text' — the museum quality is visual only.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Corners are square to 2px at most. No pill shapes, no rounded cards.

dos: Do use framed plates (paper + plate shadow) to present featured output.
Do maintain the ~62ch measure for running text.
Do use Newsreader for display and body reading text, Archivo for UI, headings, and labels.
donts: Don't load Tailwind from a CDN, or any external font or script.
Don't name sections or UI elements metaphorically ('exhibits,' 'wall text,' 'desks').
Don't use pill badges or rounded cards.
Don't use pure black (#000) for text — ink (#131312) is the floor.
